status: One bounded source-fit civic-action design using an unchanged shared claim. Other Grade 5 records remain under review; no learner attainment is inferred.

completed-school-action.title: Kensington CS Students Mark Earth Day with Community Cleanup
completed-school-action.reviewed: Complete main body; no photo copied or visual observation claimed.
completed-school-action.supports: A dated school/community group worked together on 22 April to remove litter and reported three bags collected.
completed-school-action.limits: One reported action, not proof that all litter or pollution disappeared. Counts are not a long-term ecological effect or learner assessment record.

current-volunteer-actions.reviewed: Complete main body and opportunity table.
current-volunteer-actions.supports: Examples include ecological stewardship, public-service feedback and helping at community services.
current-volunteer-actions.limits: Programme roles/age eligibility differ; the packet teaches about these actions and does not enrol a child in an adult or 14–18 role.

campaign-and-provider-roles.supports: Distinct residents/groups/City coordination and public-litter reporting as well as staff work.
campaign-and-provider-roles.limits: The release’s staff-collected total is not attributed to school volunteers; an invitation is not evidence of the later event’s outcome. No superlative or participation estimate is required knowledge.

actions: Prepare original short source-attributed summaries of the completed Kensington action and current City opportunities. Retain actual dates and distinguish citizens, school/community groups, government staff and a provider programme. The school case is a particular completed civic/environmental action; programme advertisements or invitations are not claims of completed success.

Have the learner explain who worked together, their shared civic aim and why the actions were suitable. Identify supported achievement in the school case without inflating three reported bags into a solved environmental problem or confusing it with City crews’ separate collected total. The class’s comprehension is assessed; no source photo or child record is reproduced.

Use the current opportunities to describe different ways citizens can address environmental and social issues: volunteering to care for shared places, supporting community services, offering public-service feedback, or jointly advocating for an accessible class/community resource. Explain how a letter, petition, organised volunteering or awareness activity could contribute to a stated aim. No exhaustive list of illustrative source examples is required.

Retain the whole existing claim by planning a class campaign for a clearly labelled original scenario, for example improving access to a shared reading/play resource. Identify the issue, shared values, intended audience, two possible action methods, the chosen method and why it fits, roles and a realistic way to check progress. Draft or simulate a letter/poster/petition where useful; no sending, signature collection, enrolment or actual political participation is needed for this source/task design.

Use a changed social or environmental problem to test transfer. Distinguish what citizens can do from what needs a responsible authority’s decision; do not promise that a petition automatically makes law or that every person can use every programme. A justified explanation and plan matter, not political agreement, emotion, popularity or speed.
citizens-take-action.positive: Explains the completed collective action and different suitable citizen methods across social/environmental issues, then creates a justified campaign plan with shared goal and roles.
nearMiss: Names an isolated kind act but cannot explain joint action toward a civic goal.
Calls an invitation or volunteering advert a completed achievement.
Attributes City staff outcomes to children or claims a local activity solved all pollution.
Offers one method for every problem without audience, consequences or a plan.
citizens-take-action.contributionRole: Existing whole civic-goal operation plus the original source-fit task accounts for B3.9; source facts and task design complement the association rather than infer pupil mastery.

readinessBoundary.policy: Hard prerequisites remain unchanged and are assessed/selected separately. Missing local contexts and the prerequisite’s actual participation/interview performance are readiness matters; they are not silently added as mandatory B3.9 source requirements or satisfied through this link. No country association is fabricated just to close a path.
